key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation follows different solid-state conversion routes in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so bandgap control must be tuned to the specific precursor chemistry.
engineering_relevance: This enables solvent-free, scalable fabrication of all-perovskite tandem solar cells with improved efficiency and thermal stability.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compared mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG conversion pathways during deposition and annealing
Used the mechanistic insights to optimize sTE absorbers across 1.26–1.96 eV
evidence_signal: The optimized evaporated tandem achieved 19.2% power conversion efficiency and retained about 80% of initial efficiency after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Vertical compositional gradients and incomplete interdiffusion in NBG absorbers may still limit reproducibility and long-term uniformity.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
